contribution.value: AQLM extends classic Additive Quantization (a multi-codebook method from information retrieval) to LLM weight compression, achieving Pareto-optimal accuracy below 3 bits per parameter and strong results in the 2-bit regime, with practical GPU/CPU kernels.

ev.quote: Our algorithm, called AQLM, generalizes the classic Additive Quantization (AQ) approach for information retrieval to advance the state-of-the-art in LLM compression, via two innovations: 1) learned additive quantization of weight matrices in input-adaptive fashion, and 2) joint optimization of codebook parameters across each transformer blocks.

strengths.value: First scheme to be Pareto optimal below 3 bits per parameter, beating QuIP# and prior baselines across LLAMA 2 7B/13B/70B at 2-3 bit budgets.

ev.quote: AQLM is the first scheme that is Pareto optimal in terms of accuracy-vs-model-size when compressing to less than 3 bits per parameter, and significantly improves upon all known schemes in the extreme compression (2bit) regime.

strengths.value: Provides fast GPU and CPU kernels that match or beat FP16 latency, with up to x4 CPU speedup and around 14 tokens/s on LLAMA 2 70B.

ev.quote: we provide fast GPU and CPU implementations of AQLM for token generation, which enable us to match or outperform optimized FP16 implementations for speed

strengths.value: Uses a homogeneous quantized format with no sparse outlier matrix, making it simpler to deploy than mixed sparse-quantized methods like SpQR.

ev.quote: Unlike some extreme LLM quantization approaches that require hybrid sparse-quantized formats which separate outlier quantization (Kim et al., 2023; Dettmers et al., 2023b), AQLM quantizes models in a simple homogeneous format, which is easy to support in practice.

strengths.value: Open-source GitHub release of code and quantized checkpoints supports reproducibility.

ev.quote: We share the code for our method in the GitHub repository https://github.com/Vahe1994/AQLM/tree/AQLM_camera_ready.

weaknesses.value: More compute-expensive than direct PTQ methods like RTN or GPTQ because of the more complex coding representation.

ev.quote: AQLM is more computationally-expensive than direct post-training quantization methods, such as RTN or GPTQ, specifically because of the use of a more complex coding representation.

weaknesses.value: Strict 2-bit AQLM is not Pareto optimal for the same model; only the 2.5-bit point becomes Pareto optimal.

ev.quote: AQLM compression to strictly 2 bits for the same model is also below Pareto-optimality, as it is outperformed by 4-bit AQLM compression for LLAMA 2 7B (5.21 vs 5.59).

weaknesses.value: Beam search picked for codes is not the fastest MRF solver; randomized ICM could be faster but was not implemented.

ev.quote: Note that beam search is not necessarily the best solution to this problem. AQ variants for retrieval ... use randomized ICM to find solutions faster.

weaknesses.value: Codebook update uses Adam as a workaround instead of a closed-form least-squares solver, leaving extra hyperparameters in the loop.

ev.quote: For simplicity, our current implementation defaults to using Adam (Kingma & Ba, 2015) for approximately solving this minimization problem ... In future work, these hyperparameters could be eliminated by switching to dedicated least squares solver

limitations.value: No safety, bias, refusal, or jailbreak evaluation after extreme compression; only PPL and zero-shot accuracy are reported.

ev.quote: We report perplexity on WikiText-2 (Merity et al., 2016) and C4 (Raffel et al., 2020) validation sets. We also measure zero-shot accuracy on WinoGrande

limitations.value: Calibration and inference run on data-centre GPUs (A100/H100) and a desktop RTX 3090; no edge or mobile hardware tested.

ev.quote: In all of our experiments, we used either Nvidia A100 or H100 ... To evaluate inference speed on GPU we used consumer-grade GPU Nvidia 3090

limitations.value: Tested only on LLAMA 2 base models and Mixtral; no instruction-tuned or chat variants are evaluated.

ev.quote: Our evaluation is focused on the LLAMA 2 model family since it is a popular backbone for fine-tuned models or general LLM applications, e.g. (Dettmers et al., 2023a), and we also present results on Mistral-family models

limitations.value: No long-context evaluation; calibration uses 4096-token windows and benchmarks rely on standard PPL/zero-shot tasks.

ev.quote: We calibrate each algorithm using the subset of RedPajama dataset (Computer, 2023), with a sequence length of 4096.

future_work_stated.value: Explore better fine-tuning strategies for compressed models (e.g. PV-tuning) to further close the accuracy gap at 2-3 bits.

ev.quote: we found that better fine-tuning algorithms (Tseng et al., 2024; Malinovskii et al., 2024) can significantly improve quantized model accuracy. We believe that AQLM can benefit from a more systematic exploration of fine-tuning algorithms

future_work_stated.value: Generalise AQLM to other quantization scenarios such as computer vision models and KV-cache compression for long sequences.

ev.quote: the underlying algorithm can potentially be adapted to other problems, e.g. quantizing computer vision models, compressing LLM attention caches for long sequences, and others.

future_work_stated.value: Replace Adam-based codebook update with a dedicated least-squares solver to remove tuning hyperparameters.

ev.quote: In future work, these hyperparameters could be eliminated by switching to dedicated least squares solver for codebooks.
we revisit the problem of "extreme" LLM compression—defined as targeting extremely low bit counts, such as 2 to 3 bits per parameter
